<template id="tpl-image-to-ascii">
<fieldset>
    <div style="width: 100%; overflow: hidden; background-color: black;">
        <pre style="background-color: black; color: white" id="ascii-output">No image to show.</pre>
    </div>
    <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap:10px;">
        <input type="file" id="file-input" accept="image/" style="display: none;">
        <input type="text" id="file-name-display" readonly placeholder="No file selected">
        <button onclick="document.getElementById('file-input').click()">Browse...</button>
    </div>
    <div>
        <label style="font-size:20px;"><val id="width-value"></val>Size</label>
        <input type="range" id="width" class="slider" min="40" max="200" value="200">
    </div>
    <div>
        <label style="font-size:20px;"><val id="contrast-value"></val>Contrast</label>
        <input type="range" id="contrast" class="slider" min="0" max="200" value="100">
    </div>
    <div>
        <label style="font-size:20px;" for="depth"><val id="depth-value"></val>Depth</label>
        <input type="range" id="depth" min=1 max=6 value=4 step=1>
    </div>
    <div style="display: grid; gap: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px;">
        <span style="font-size: 20px;">Edge Behavior</span>
        <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; gap:10px; justify-content: space-around;">
            <input type="radio" id="edge-none" name="edge-choice" checked>
            <label style="font-size: 20px;" for="edge-none">None</label>
            <input type="radio" id="edge-detect" name="edge-choice">
            <label style="font-size: 20px;" for="edge-detect">Detect</label>
            <input type="radio" id="edge-enhance" name="edge-choice">
            <label style="font-size: 20px;" for="edge-enhance">Enhance</label>
        </div>
    </div>
    <div style="display:flex; justify-content: center; gap: 20px;">
        <button style="width:fit-content" py-click="run">Convert</button>
        <button style="width:fit-content" onclick="navigator.clipboard.writeText(document.getElementById('ascii-output').textContent)">Copy</button>
    </div>
</fieldset>
<span style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 1.2rem;text-align: left; white-space: pre-wrap;">
<p>This tool is written in Python and uses several methods of image manipulation using the <a href="https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/">pillow</a> library.</p>

<p>First the image is resized based on the width parameter. A magic number of 2.2 is used to account for the difference in height and width of the monospace font.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; width: 100%;">def resize_image(image, new_width):
    image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)
    width, height = image.size
    ratio = height / (2.2 * width)
    new_height = int(new_width * ratio)
    return image.resize((new_width, new_height))</code>

<p>Next contrast is applied. This is especially important if no edge detection parameter is selected.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; width: 100%;">def change_contrast(img, level=100):
    factor = 259*(level+255)/255*(259-level)
    def contrast(c):
        return 128 + factor * (c-128)
    return img.point(contrast)</code>

<p>Then, color information is removed from the image. We really only need the brightness information for the ASCII representation.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; width: 100%;">def grayify(image):
    return image.convert("L")</code>

<p>And the edges are optionally detected and enhanced.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; width: 100%;">def detect_edges(image, edge_behavior: str):
    behaviors = {
        "edge-detect": ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES,
        "edge-enhance": ImageFilter.EDGE_ENHANCE,
        "edge-none": None
    }
    behavior = behaviors.get(edge_behavior)

    if behavior: return image.filter(behavior)
    return image</code>

<p>The pixels are then converted to ASCII characters based on their brightness. The character set is determined by the depth parameter. Each set is ordered based on perceived brightness, and the character set is indexed accordingly.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; overflow-x: scroll; text-wrap: nowrap;">def pixels_to_ascii(image, depth):
    pixels = image.getdata()
    ascii_list = [
        list(" @"),
        list(" /9@"),
        list(" ^/([9$@"),
        list(" .-^/T(f[j9K$M@"),
        list(" `.-':^;!/zTJ(if3[5jwk9OK8$0M%@"),
        list(""" `.-':_^=;>!c*/zsTv)J(Fi{fI31t[ne5Yxja]wqkP9d4pOAKXm8D$Bg0MQ%&@""")
    ]
    ASCII_CHARS = ascii_list[depth - 1]
    characters = "".join(ASCII_CHARS[p // (256 // len(ASCII_CHARS))] for p in pixels)
    return characters</code>

<p>Finally, the above functions are combined and the lines of text are joined on newlines.</p>

<code style="padding: 10px; width: 100%;">def convert_image_from_bytes(image_bytes,
                             depth,
                             new_width,
                             contrast,
                             edge_behavior):

    image = Image.open(BytesIO(image_bytes))
    image = resize_image(image, new_width)
    image = change_contrast(image, contrast)
    image = grayify(image)
    image = detect_edges(image, edge_behavior)
    ascii_data = pixels_to_ascii(image, depth)
    pixel_count = len(ascii_data)
    ascii_image = "\n".join(
        ascii_data[i:i + new_width]
        for i in range(0, pixel_count, new_width)
    )

    return ascii_image</code>

<p>The full python script can be found here: <a href="/static/python/image_to_ascii.py" target="_blank">image_to_ascii.py</a></p>
</span>
</template>

<template id="tpl-bmg-format">
<p style="text-align: left; margin: 0 0 10px 0;">Welcome to the BMG CSV Formatter. This tool is used for converting a CSV file into a TXT file format that can be imported into a BMG FluoStar OMEGA plate reader control program. CSV files should be formatted like a 96-well plate. The first column should have the letters A-H, and the top row should have the numbers 1-12. Be sure to input a value for each well you are using even if there are duplicate entries.</p>
<div style="display: grid; gap: 10px;">
    <div class="field-row" style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-around;">
        <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; align-items: center;">
            <input type="file" id="file-input" accept=".csv" style="display: none;">
            <input type="text" id="file-name-display" readonly placeholder="No file selected" style="width:fit-content">
            <button onclick="document.getElementById('file-input').click()">Browse...</button>
            <button py-click="run_bmg">Format</button>
        </div>
    </div>
    <pre id="bmg-preview" style="max-height: 400px; overflow: scroll;"></pre>
    <button id="download-btn" disabled>Download TXT File</button>
</div>
</template>

        <span style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 1.2rem;text-align: left; white-space: pre-wrap;">
Gage Rowden 2026

This tool simulates the rolling mechanics of the Legends of the 5 Rings role-playing game.

The user chooses a number of ten-sided dice to roll and a number less than or equal to that number of dice to keep. The tool calculates the probability of achieving a target number of successes, and visualizes the results.

Upon opening, the tool simulates 10,000 rolls for each possible roll/keep combination. The probability is shown as both a proportion of successes to losses (empirical) and as the area of the estimated density curve (calculated).

The tool was written in Python, and the core logic of the roller is implemented in the following "roll_dice()" function, which uses a recursive approach to determine the final roll.
                                            <code style="width: 100%;">def roll_dice(roll, keep):
    assert roll >= keep, "roll must be ≥ keep."
    rolls = [randint(1,10) for _ in range(roll)]
    keeps = sorted(rolls)[::-1][:keep]
    for i in keeps:
        if i != 10: break
        keeps += roll_dice(1, 1)
    return keeps</code>
The function first generates a list of length "roll" of random integers between 1 and 10. The rolls are sorted in descending order, and the first "keep" amount of numbers are chosen. If any "keeps" equal 10, the function is called again with roll=1 and keep=1. This goes on until no more 10's are rolled.
        </span>
    </div>
</div>
